messages.subject: Regularization p. 401 manual version 2.6
parts:
Dear all,

I have problems to understand, why, lambda the shrinkage is independent from N the number of objects.

(beta_hat, sigma_hat) = ... 

If I look into glmnet manual page 10. http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/glmnet/glmnet.pdf

the loglik is devided by nobs (N in our case). In STAN I could do the same by adding "* N" to the 
statement result in:

increment_log_prob(- lambda * dot_self(beta) * N);

Another problem I have is, if the design matrix x contains '0', thus beta corresponding beta is "ignored",
but we still add beta^2 increment_log_prob. Is this correct? 

Thank you,
Andre

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Regularization p. 401 manual version 2.6
parts:
> On Feb 25, 2015, at 7:23 AM, andre.p...@googlemail.com wrote:
>
> Dear all,
>
> I have problems to understand, why, lambda the shrinkage is independent from N the number of objects.
>
> (beta_hat, sigma_hat) = ...
We don't usually use data-dependent priors.

> If I look into glmnet manual page 10. http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/glmnet/glmnet.pdf
>
> the loglik is devided by nobs (N in our case).

I'm not familiar with glmnet, but I took a look and
indeed that's what they seem to be doing.

> In STAN [Stan] I could do the same by adding "* N" to the

> statement result in:
>
> increment_log_prob(- lambda * dot_self(beta) * N);

Yes, that will give you the same result if the likelihood and
shrinkage are your only terms.

> Another problem I have is, if the design matrix x contains '0', thus beta corresponding beta is "ignored",
> but we still add beta^2 increment_log_prob. Is this correct?
>

Yes, that's correct.

If an entire column of x is 0, then adding -lambda * beta^2 will
cause beta to go to 0. A better solution is to just drop the column
of the matrix.

- Bob
